captions.instagram:
What are electric current and voltage?

Current is a flow of charge, voltage is the push behind it. Build a torch and count the electrons, light fairy lights in series and in parallel, switch on a geyser and an AC in an Indian home, drain a phone and an electric car, and find out why a bird on a wire is safe but wet hands are not.

→ Current is charge per second. Voltage is the energy each coulomb carries: 1.5 volts per cell.
→ Electrons crawl at 0.1 mm a second, but the push races round the loop near light speed.
→ In parallel, each bulb gets the full voltage. A short circuit sends a huge current and the fuse melts.
→ Indian mains is 230 volts AC: the push flips direction 50 times every second.
→ A 2 kW geyser draws 8.7 amps. If current leaks to earth, the RCCB cuts it in milliseconds.

In this video:
• Flow and push. Current is charge flowing past a point each second, I = Q ÷ t, in amperes.
• Series and parallel. Bulbs in series share the voltage and all go out if one breaks, like old fairy lights.
• Home electricity. Indian mains is 230 V AC at 50 Hz; the US uses 120 V at 60 Hz.
• Batteries and power. A cell turns chemical energy into electrical energy: 1.5 V for an AA, 3.7 V for lithium-ion, 12 V for six lead-acid cells, nearly 400 V for an EV pack.
• Safety and myths. Current, not voltage alone, harms you: about 1 mA is felt, 10 mA can stop you letting go, 100 mA can kill.
